topic: Mugil IDE: Token-Efficient Browser-Based Autonomous Coding Agent

key_points: Open source AI coding agent built for the terminal (TUI), ~200k GitHub stars
Established agentic function-calling loop with workspace tools and MCP consumption
Terminal-first UX; Mugil IDE explicitly positions itself as browser-only alternative
Mugil's tool loop and MCP client are directly inspired by OpenCode patterns
CLI proxy that reduces LLM token consumption by 60-90% on common dev commands
Single Rust binary, zero dependencies, ~77k stars
Boilerplate stripping and command-output compression — the same idea Mugil's RTK module implements
Proxy/CLI approach vs Mugil's in-engine prompt-refinement approach
Terse, filler-free prompt compression — the direct inspiration for Mugil's Caveman module
Focus on stripping conversational filler to cut token cost
Standalone tool vs Mugil's integrated pipeline module
Strips AI provenance watermarks (invisible Unicode carriers, vendor attribution lines)
Direct inspiration for Mugil's Watermark Remover module
Addresses the 'AI-generated code signature' problem in output
Using static analysis to reduce token usage of AI coding agents
Shows code retrieval/context reduction is a major lever for token efficiency
Parallels Mugil's Codegraph module which gives the agent exact code in one call

stats.fact: Mugil IDE is an open-source (MIT), browser-only autonomous AI IDE; latest npm version 0.1.6, requires Node.js >= 20
mugil-ide npm package had 845 downloads in the last week (2026-08-15 to 2026-08-21); @mugil-ide/core had 950
Mugil IDE ships 335 unit tests and 16 workspace tools (read_file, write_file, edit_file, apply_patch, run_command, codegraph, webfetch, websearch, lsp, task, etc.)

Mugil's token-efficiency pipeline: signature strip -> token refinement (caveman + rtk + truncate) -> cache lookup -> model routing/handoff -> cache store, with Ponytail output-minimization injected into the system prompt
Mugil's Smart Cache supports exact -> partial (prefix+delta) -> semantic (embedding similarity) tiers with memory/Redis/file backends and TTL, scoped per requested model

Mugil supports 10+ providers via Auto Handoff: OpenRouter (primary), OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel AI Gateway, Cloudflare Workers AI, Together AI, OpenCode Zen, Ollama, LM Studio, and generic local endpoints, with cost-based routing and fallback chains
RTK (Reduced Token Kernel), a direct inspiration for Mugil's RTK module, claims to reduce LLM token consumption by 60-90% on common dev commands
OpenCode, the terminal-based coding agent that inspired Mugil's tool loop, has ~200k GitHub stars

Dan Luu's analysis found a 2.6x token-efficiency gap between C (least efficient) and Clojure (most efficient) among programming languages, with array languages like J even more efficient (~70 tokens avg)

angles: Browser-only autonomous IDE as a differentiator vs terminal-first agents (OpenCode, Claude Code) — no TUI, no CLI, all interaction in the browser with xterm.js two-pane UI
Token efficiency as the core value prop: prompt refinement (Caveman/RTK), output minimization (Ponytail), aggressive multi-tier caching, and signature/watermark stripping
The credited-module architecture: Mugil is a composition of proven open-source ideas (caveman, rtk, ponytail, watermarks-remover, codegraph, OpenCode patterns) rather than a from-scratch engine
Cost-based model routing across 10+ providers with fallback chains and an explicitly-selected-model-is-authoritative rule (no silent ladder fallback)
Offline-first: vendored xterm.js assets mean an installed client runs fully offline — no CDN, no Node-gyp surprises
Safety/permission model: /plan (read-only) vs /act (asks first) modes, browser approval modal, per-mode tool permission overrides
MCP dual role: exposes the engine as an MCP server AND consumes MCP servers as agent tools — a bridge between token-efficient pipeline and the broader MCP ecosystem
Early-stage project (0.1.x, ~2 GitHub stars, <1k weekly npm downloads) — a review of a promising but immature tool
